Alto saxophonist Lanny Morgan was born on March 30, 1934 in DesMoines, Iowa. His family moved to Los Angeles in 1944 and he gained big band experience at Los Angeles City College. He worked locally and on the road with the bands of Charlie Barnet, Si Zentner and Terry Gibbs and in 1960 traveled to New York to join Maynard Ferguson’s band. Lanny was one of the principal soloists with this group, recording frequently and touring Europe in 1962. He has led an active career in west coast studios while performing with Bill Berry, Ed Shaughnessy, Bill Holman and SuperSax.
Lanny was interviewed in Los Angeles on February 14, 1999, by Monk Rowe, Director of the Hamilton College Jazz Archive.

My name is Monk Rowe. We are filming for the Hamilton College Jazz Archive in Los Angeles. And this is a real pleasure for me to welcome the man with the meanest alto sound this side of Marshall Royal. Lanny Morgan. Welcome.
Thank you. Thanks for having me. It’s nice to be here.
I recall hearing your sound on albums dating quite a while back so this is a pleasure.
